decisions.old_printed_clause: ἐὰν οὖν ὁ ὀφείλων ἀγαθοποιεῖν πονηρεύηται
decisions.new_selected_clause: ἐὰν οὖν ὁ ἀγαπῶν ἀγαθοποιεῖν πονηρεύηται
decisions.damage: The finalι/ν of αγαθοποιειν are dotted as uncertain. Neither the love verb nor the infinitive is inside supplied or a correction apparatus.
decisions.rationale: Prefer the early continuous Greek reading “who loves to do good” over the older version-based conjecture “who ought to do good.” The reported Athos “who loves greatly” also preserves the love verb, though corrupt; the Latin/Ethiopic-based conjecture remains an explicit alternative. This is not wholesale adoption of Sinaiticus or its spelling.
English_alternatives: If someone who loves to do good does evil, does that person not seem to do greater evil than someone who does not know God?
If someone who ought to do good does evil, does that person not seem to do greater evil than someone who does not know God?
